1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 180-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V_K, if W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K (the action rho of the Chevalley generators of L_K), then W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

parameters.type: complex Lie algebra representation of L on V

hypotheses.statement: The field K has characteristic p.
With the representation act, V=V(lambda) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl2(C)-module of highest weight lambda and has complex dimension lambda+1.
L=sl2(C), and x,y,h are its Chevalley generators, satisfying [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h.
v is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=lambda v.

M is an admissible lattice in V: it is a free abelian subgroup possessing an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. M is arbitrary and is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

definitions.type: family of elements of the universal enveloping algebra U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: X_r=x^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with X_0=1. U(L) is the complex associative enveloping algebra of L. Elements of U(L) act on V through the extension of act. Juxtaposition such as xv denotes this action.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(L), indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: Y_r=y^r/r! for every integer r>=0, with Y_0=1, acting on V via act.
U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra of U(L) generated by X_r and Y_r for every integer r>=0.
n=lambda+1.
I={i in Z: 0<=i<=lambda}.

definitions.type: family of vectors of V indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: e_i=y^i v/i!=Y_i v for integers i>=0; only indices in I are used for the candidate basis.

definitions.type: subring of Q and hence of C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b in Q: a,b are integers and p does not divide b}. Ring operations are those of Q. All R-actions on submodules of V or C below use this inclusion.
M_R=R tensor_Z M, with scalar multiplication on the R factor.
iota(r tensor m)=r m in V, extended by the balanced tensor universal property. The R-module structure of V is restriction of complex scalars.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by I times I
definitions.definition: For i,j in I, E_ij is the unique complex linear operator sending e_j to e_i and sending e_k to 0 for every k in I with k!=j. It is defined using the complex basis (e_i) indexed by I.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i in I, J_i={c in C: c e_i belongs to iota(M_R)}.
J={c in C: c e_0 belongs to iota(M_R)}. When 0 belongs to I this is J_0; the definition does not assume that the different J_i agree.
V_K=V(K)=M tensor_Z K, with K acting on the K factor.
L_K=L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh) tensor_Z K, with bracket induced by [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h. These integral bracket formulas define the Chevalley construction including in characteristic 2.

definitions.type: K-linear Lie algebra representation of L_K on V_K
definitions.definition: rho is the action induced by the lattice operators: for t in {x,y,h}, rho(t tensor 1)(m tensor c)=(tm) tensor c, extended K-linearly to L_K. The action is defined when the lattice operators preserve M and satisfy the Chevalley relations.
x_K=rho(x tensor 1).
y_K=rho(y tensor 1).
h_K=rho(h tensor 1).

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: X_r^K, also denoted (X_K)_r, is induced by X_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (X_r m) tensor c.

definitions.type: family of K-linear endomorphisms of V_K indexed by natural r
definitions.definition: Y_r^K, also denoted (Y_K)_r, is induced by Y_r on M tensor_Z K: m tensor c maps to (Y_r m) tensor c.
F_p=Z/pZ with its field structure for the prime p. For K of characteristic p its canonical embedding in K sends the residue class of an integer to that integer times 1_K.

value.representation_notes:
Use the concrete complex trace-zero 2×2 matrix Lie algebra Reduction.SL for the source's L=sl2(C), with a Lie homomorphism act into complex endomorphisms and an arbitrary generating Chevalley triple x,y,h. The pinned IsSl2Triple includes h≠0 and the three commutator relations; the span condition says the triple generates the whole complex Lie algebra. H004 retains finite dimension, nonzeroness, irreducibility under every Lie element and existence of a highest-weight vector of weight l; H006 fixes the source's chosen vector. The prime p is represented by a natural number, equivalently the original positive prime integer; the weight l remains an integer. Under H003, Ind l=Fin(l.toNat+1) is exactly the ordered set of integers 0≤i≤l. basisFacts explicitly retains nonnegativity and l+1>0, so later consumers do not rely on an unstated conversion. Fin indices are natural positions, subtraction in divided-power indices is truncated natural subtraction in regions where it equals the source's nonnegative integer difference. Complex weights such as l−2i use signed casts.
M is an arbitrary integer submodule of V, equivalently an additive subgroup. admissible expresses an integer basis whose inclusions form a complex basis and preservation by all divided powers. Preservation by these generators is equivalent to preservation by their unital integer algebra U_Z. No special choice of lattice is built into a definition. divided is the action of x^r/r! or y^r/r! as a complex endomorphism, using endomorphism multiplication as composition. matrixUnit b i j sends w to its j-th basis coordinate times b_i. It is only used with an actual basis whose values equal the source e_i; no basis is selected by an unproved definition.
loc p is the subring of Q generated by inverses of integers prime to p. The typed locSpec obligation in T003 identifies it with the exact fractions a/d, p∤d from D007; this identification is proved, not assumed. The composite inclusion loc p→Q→C gives all localized actions. MR is R⊗_Z M, and iota is the balanced multiplication map from LinearMap.liftBaseChange. Jcoord is the inverse image of its range under c↦c e_i; rationalMu is multiplication Q⊗_R J→C. coordinateFacts gives the exact direct-sum isomorphism with its sum formula, rationalFacts includes finite dimensionality as well as finrank=1 and injectivity, and principalFacts supplies the scalar b and actual localized basis. Module.finrank is Cardinal.toNat of rank: it is used as dimension only with the explicit finite basis or finite-dimensional conditions.
Use the standard scalar-first tensor convention VK=K⊗_Z M throughout. The source writes M⊗_Z K; the canonical symmetry sends c⊗m to m⊗c, identifies K scalar multiplication on the first factor with that on the second, and identifies f.baseChange K with the source action on pure tensors. This is an order convention for one representation, not a second independent model. T008 explicitly constructs the source's substantive scalar-extension and reduction bridges, in this convention. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the range of integer multiplication by p, which is exactly pMR, with its canonical ZMod p module. The existential ring homomorphisms bar and eps supply the actual R and prime-field scalar actions on K; they are conclusions, never premise instances. Pure-tensor forward and inverse formulas and intertwining obligations fix the meanings of both bridges.
IntegralOps contains only integer-linear restrictions with equality to the complex operators after inclusion; existence is proved in T003. Their components are unique by injectivity of inclusion of M, so all compatible bundles induce the same operators on VK. This avoids any definition choosing restrictions before their existence is proved. reductionFacts quantifies over every compatible bundle and supplies the basis, matrix units, nonzero binomials and factorial power identities. Invariant subspaces are actual Submodule K objects; stable means closure under the stated operator. The endpoint existentially supplies the canonical restriction bundle, nonzeroness and the complete zero-or-top assertion. No Lie algebra of trace-zero matrices over K is substituted for the integral Chevalley construction: in characteristic two the three integral generators are still the ones whose induced actions occur here.

steps.statement: Reduction.strings l (act x) (act y) (act h) v0
steps.explanation: Prove the two natural inductions in order. The representation Lie homomorphism sends brackets to operator commutators; complete the h induction before using it in the x step. The x formula is asserted only for t≥1.

steps.statement: Reduction.basisFacts l (act x) (act y) (act h) v0
steps.explanation: N001 in full. Establish nonzero e_i by repeated raising; use the product of h−weight operators over the other indices to isolate coefficients and then the dimension hypothesis for a basis. Exclude the extra weight to terminate the lowering string. Normalize and iterate to obtain the generator and natural binomial formulas. The predicates retain signed-weight and endpoint conventions.

steps.statement: Reduction.latticeFacts p l (act x) (act y) (act h) M
steps.explanation: Build the compatible integer restrictions from admissibility; obtain h from xy−yx and retain the commutator identities. Prove locSpec from the ring generated by prime-to-p inverses (finite sums/products of fractions). Tensor an admissible integer basis, identify the localized coordinates, prove iota injective, its complex span, finite free rank and stability of its image.

steps.statement: Reduction.localizationFacts p l (act x) (act y) (act h) v0 M
steps.explanation: N002 in full, retaining T003. For a basis with values e_i prove Q=Y_l X_l and the two adjacent matrix-unit identities by their action on that basis. The prime-to-p factorial calculation proves the binomial is a unit of R and that its rational inverse is in R. Compose to obtain every matrix unit and its lattice preservation. Quantification over matching bases prevents dependence on an arbitrary new basis choice.

steps.statement: Reduction.coordinateFacts p l (act y) v0 M
steps.explanation: Project to J_i e_i and transfer coordinates with E_ij to prove equality of all J_i. Finite generators descend along coordinate projections; nonzeroness follows from the complex span. Assemble the coordinate inclusions into the stated isomorphism, with its precise sum formula and inverse projections.

Use common rational denominators to prove multiplication Q⊗_R J→C injective, and finite generators for finite dimensionality. Tensor the coordinate decomposition; apply the pinned Module.finrank_baseChange with S=loc p, R=Q, M'=MR, and Module.finrank_pi_fintype over Q for the constant finite family Q⊗_R J indexed by Ind l. The inspected StrongRankCondition means an injective linear map (Fin a→R)→(Fin b→R) forces a≤b; it is not a finiteness or freeness assumption. Supply freeness and finite generation separately from the actual bases and finite-dimensional spaces, and strong rank condition from the commutative domains. Use the pinned library declarations directly, with no M premise ports. Finrank is Cardinal.toNat of rank, and these spaces have explicitly finite bases. The equality n=n*r with n>0 gives r=1.

steps.statement: Reduction.commonFacts p l (act y) v0 M
steps.explanation: N003 in full, retaining coordinate and rational facts. In the one-dimensional rational line choose a nonzero a and express finite generators as nonzero rational multiples. Factor each as p^eta times a unit of loc p, take the minimum exponent and construct b. Prove J=Rb and obtain the localized basis with the explicit iota images; retain all witnesses inside the existential output.

Construct bar and the canonical prime-field map eps. Prove the two K-linear tensor equivalences with the declared forward/inverse formulas, using balancing and p=0. ModN is exactly the quotient by pMR. For each integer endomorphism, prove the naturality equations; construct its descended ZMod-linear quotient map with the stated quotient formula. This gives intertwining for x,y,h and every divided power without extra action premises.

steps.statement: Reduction.reductionFacts p l K (act x) (act y) (act h) M
steps.explanation: N004 in full. Choose b and the basis a from N003 and transport the scalar extensions through the explicit equivalences. Transport N001's generator coefficients and N002's matrix units. A unital map sends the binomial units to units of K. Prove r! nonzero for r≤l

steps.statement: Reduction.invariantFacts p l K (act x) (act y) (act h) M
steps.explanation: The positive finite basis gives nonzeroness. For each compatible restriction bundle choose the basis and T from N004. Under the three invariance assumptions, close W under nonnegative powers, scalar multiples and compositions. The factorial formulas and nonzero binomial make every T_ij preserve W. Retain these very witnesses together with their reductionWitness properties for the continuation.

steps.statement: Reduction.endpoint K (act x) (act y) (act h) M
steps.explanation: Choose the compatible restrictions guaranteed by N002, then the witnesses retained by T010. Split W=0 versus W≠0. In the nonzero branch choose a nonzero coordinate of a vector; apply T_ij and divide by that coordinate to put every beta_i in W. Discharge the cases and invariance assumptions and quantify W. The source conclusion is invariance under the integral Chevalley generators; their span identifies this with the full Lie-submodule assertion, including p=2 and l=0.

import Mathlib
universe u v
open scoped TensorProduct
open Module
attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing
noncomputable section
namespace Reduction
def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
  Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
  ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
  K ⊗[ℤ] M
variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype

abbrev SL := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
def stable {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (U : Submodule A W) (f : Module.End A W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def matrixUnit {A W ι : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (b : Basis ι A W) (i j : ι) : Module.End A W :=
  LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i)
def Jcoord (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (loc p) ℂ :=
  (iota p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[loc p] ℂ) (e y v i))
structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
  ix : Module.End ℤ M
  iy : Module.End ℤ M
  ih : Module.End ℤ M
  iX : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
  ix_spec : ∀ m : M, (ix m : V) = x m
  iy_spec : ∀ m : M, (iy m : V) = y m
  ih_spec : ∀ m : M, (ih m : V) = h m
  iX_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iX r m : V) = divided x r m
  iY_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iY r m : V) = divided y r m
def admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (a : Basis ι ℤ M) (b : Basis ι ℂ V),
    ∀ i, (a i : V) = b i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), divided x r m ∈ M ∧ divided y r m ∈ M)
def highestModule (l : ℤ) (act : SL →ₗ⁅ℂ⁆ Module.End ℂ V) (x h : SL) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
  (∀ U : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ z : SL, stable U (act z)) → U = ⊥ ∨ U = ⊤) ∧
  ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ act x w = 0 ∧ act h w = (l : ℂ) • w
def chevalley (x y h : SL) : Prop :=
  IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x, y, h} : Set SL) = ⊤
def strings (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → x ((y ^ t) v) =
    ((t : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • (y ^ (t - 1)) v
def generatorFormulas {A W : Type*} [Field A] [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End A W) (f : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  x (f 0) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → x (f (i+1)) = ((l : A) - (i : A)) • f i) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → y (f i) = ((i : A) + 1) • f (i+1)) ∧
  y (f l.toNat) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → h (f i) = ((l : A) - 2 * (i : A)) • f i)
def basisFacts (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 ≤ l ∧ 0 < l + 1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Ind l) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  (∃ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
  strings l x y h v ∧
  (∀ t : ℕ, l.toNat + 1 ≤ t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
  generatorFormulas l x y h (e y v) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided x r (e y v i.val) =
      if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
    divided y r (e y v i.val) =
      if i.val + r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val+r) else 0)

instance locRatComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℚ ℂ :=
  IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
def locSpec (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ loc p ↔ ∃ a d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ)
def latticeFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  locSpec p ∧ Nonempty (IntegralOps x y h M) ∧
  (∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M,
    A.ih * A.ix - A.ix * A.ih = (2 : ℤ) • A.ix ∧
    A.ih * A.iy - A.iy * A.ih = (-2 : ℤ) • A.iy ∧
    A.ix * A.iy - A.iy * A.ix = A.ih) ∧
  Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
  Nonempty (Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Module.finrank (loc p) (MR p M) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (iota p M)) = ⊤ ∧
  ∀ (r : ℕ) (z : V), z ∈ (iota p M).range →
    divided x r z ∈ (iota p M).range ∧ divided y r z ∈ (iota p M).range
def matrixFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
  ∀ i j : Ind l,
    IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : loc p) ∧
    (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ loc p ∧
    (∀ z ∈ (iota p M).range, matrixUnit b i j z ∈ (iota p M).range) ∧
    matrixUnit b i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹ •
      (divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat * divided y (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
    divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat = matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) =
      matrixUnit b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) * divided y (l.toNat-j.val) =
      (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
def localizationFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  latticeFacts p l x y h M ∧ matrixFacts p l x y v M
def coordinateFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i : Ind l, Jcoord p M y v i.val = Jcoord p M y v 0) ∧
  Jcoord p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Jcoord p M y v 0).FG ∧
  ∃ d : (Ind l → Jcoord p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[loc p] (iota p M).range,
    ∀ c, (d c : V) = ∑ i : Ind l, (c i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
def rationalMu (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  LinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ (Jcoord p M y v 0).subtype
def rationalFacts (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) ∧
  Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0)) = 1 ∧
  Function.Injective (rationalMu p y v M)
def principalFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℂ, b ≠ 0 ∧ b ∈ Jcoord p M y v 0 ∧
    Jcoord p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (loc p) ({b} : Set ℂ) ∧
    ∃ a : Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M), ∀ i, iota p M (a i) = b • e y v i.val
def commonFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  coordinateFacts p l y v M ∧ rationalFacts p y v M ∧ principalFacts p l y v M
def scalarFacts (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (bar : loc p →+* K) (eps : ZMod p →+* K),
    (∀ (a d : ℤ) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d) (r : loc p),
      (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ) → bar r = (a : K) / (d : K)) ∧
    (letI : Algebra (loc p) K := bar.toAlgebra
     letI : Algebra (ZMod p) K := eps.toAlgebra
     ∃ (Phi : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M))
       (Psi : (K ⊗[loc p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
       (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Phi (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (s : loc p) (m : M),
         Phi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] (s ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (c * bar s) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi (c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) ∧
       (∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Psi.symm (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u) = c ⊗ₜ[loc p] u) ∧
       ∀ f : Module.End ℤ M,
         Phi.toLinearMap.comp (f.baseChange K) =
           ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K).comp Phi.toLinearMap ∧
         ∃ F : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
           (∀ u : MR p M, F (ModN.mkQ p u) = ModN.mkQ p (f.baseChange (loc p) u)) ∧
           Psi.toLinearMap.comp ((f.baseChange (loc p)).baseChange K) =
             (F.baseChange K).comp Psi.toLinearMap)
def extendBasis {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
    (l : ℤ) (b : Basis (Ind l) A W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < l.toNat+1 then b ⟨i,hi⟩ else 0
def reductionWitness (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    {x y h : Module.End ℂ V} {M : Submodule ℤ V} (A : IntegralOps x y h M)
    (beta : Basis (Ind l) K (VK K M)) (T : Ind l → Ind l → Module.End K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat+1 ∧
  generatorFormulas l (A.ix.baseChange K) (A.iy.baseChange K) (A.ih.baseChange K) (extendBasis l beta) ∧
  (∀ i j k : Ind l, T i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) ∧
  (∀ i j : Ind l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    T i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹ •
      ((A.iX (l.toNat-i.val)).baseChange K * (A.iY l.toNat).baseChange K *
        (A.iX l.toNat).baseChange K * (A.iY (l.toNat-j.val)).baseChange K)) ∧
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    (A.iX r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.ix.baseChange K)^r ∧
    (A.iY r).baseChange K = (r.factorial : K)⁻¹ • (A.iy.baseChange K)^r
def reductionFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  scalarFacts p K M ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T
def invariantFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K]
    (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M, ∃ beta T, reductionWitness p l K A beta T ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → ∀ i j : Ind l, stable W (T i j)
def endpoint (K : Type*) [Field K] (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : IntegralOps x y h M, Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
    ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
      stable W (A.ix.baseChange K) → stable W (A.iy.baseChange K) →
      stable W (A.ih.baseChange K) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
end Reduction

results.value:
Use the concrete complex trace-zero 2×2 matrix Lie algebra Reduction.SL for the source's L=sl2(C), with a Lie homomorphism act into complex endomorphisms and an arbitrary generating Chevalley triple x,y,h. The pinned IsSl2Triple includes h≠0 and the three commutator relations; the span condition says the triple generates the whole complex Lie algebra. H004 retains finite dimension, nonzeroness, irreducibility under every Lie element and existence of a highest-weight vector of weight l; H006 fixes the source's chosen vector. The prime p is represented by a natural number, equivalently the original positive prime integer; the weight l remains an integer. Under H003, Ind l=Fin(l.toNat+1) is exactly the ordered set of integers 0≤i≤l. basisFacts explicitly retains nonnegativity and l+1>0, so later consumers do not rely on an unstated conversion. Fin indices are natural positions, subtraction in divided-power indices is truncated natural subtraction in regions where it equals the source's nonnegative integer difference. Complex weights such as l−2i use signed casts.
M is an arbitrary integer submodule of V, equivalently an additive subgroup. admissible expresses an integer basis whose inclusions form a complex basis and preservation by all divided powers. Preservation by these generators is equivalent to preservation by their unital integer algebra U_Z. No special choice of lattice is built into a definition. divided is the action of x^r/r! or y^r/r! as a complex endomorphism, using endomorphism multiplication as composition. matrixUnit b i j sends w to its j-th basis coordinate times b_i. It is only used with an actual basis whose values equal the source e_i; no basis is selected by an unproved definition.
loc p is the subring of Q generated by inverses of integers prime to p. The typed locSpec obligation in T003 identifies it with the exact fractions a/d, p∤d from D007; this identification is proved, not assumed. The composite inclusion loc p→Q→C gives all localized actions. MR is R⊗_Z M, and iota is the balanced multiplication map from LinearMap.liftBaseChange. Jcoord is the inverse image of its range under c↦c e_i; rationalMu is multiplication Q⊗_R J→C. coordinateFacts gives the exact direct-sum isomorphism with its sum formula, rationalFacts includes finite dimensionality as well as finrank=1 and injectivity, and principalFacts supplies the scalar b and actual localized basis. Module.finrank is Cardinal.toNat of rank: it is used as dimension only with the explicit finite basis or finite-dimensional conditions.
Use the standard scalar-first tensor convention VK=K⊗_Z M throughout. The source writes M⊗_Z K; the canonical symmetry sends c⊗m to m⊗c, identifies K scalar multiplication on the first factor with that on the second, and identifies f.baseChange K with the source action on pure tensors. This is an order convention for one representation, not a second independent model. T008 explicitly constructs the source's substantive scalar-extension and reduction bridges, in this convention. ModN(MR,p) is the quotient by the range of integer multiplication by p, which is exactly pMR, with its canonical ZMod p module. The existential ring homomorphisms bar and eps supply the actual R and prime-field scalar actions on K; they are conclusions, never premise instances. Pure-tensor forward and inverse formulas and intertwining obligations fix the meanings of both bridges.
IntegralOps contains only integer-linear restrictions with equality to the complex operators after inclusion; existence is proved in T003. Their components are unique by injectivity of inclusion of M, so all compatible bundles induce the same operators on VK. This avoids any definition choosing restrictions before their existence is proved. reductionFacts quantifies over every compatible bundle and supplies the basis, matrix units, nonzero binomials and factorial power identities. Invariant subspaces are actual Submodule K objects; stable means closure under the stated operator. The endpoint existentially supplies the canonical restriction bundle, nonzeroness and the complete zero-or-top assertion. No Lie algebra of trace-zero matrices over K is substituted for the integral Chevalley construction: in characteristic two the three integral generators are still the ones whose induced actions occur here.

result.text:
1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
175: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

All y^t v with t>=lambda+1 vanish. The generator matrices are xe_0=0; xe_i=(lambda-i+1)e_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0<=i<lambda; ye_lambda=0; he_i=(lambda-2i)e_i for i in I. For every natural r and i in I, X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) if r<=i and is zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r<=lambda and is zero otherwise. All these coefficients are integers.

M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. Every X_r,Y_r preserves iota(M_R). For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). In particular Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda), X_(lambda-i)E_(lambda,lambda)=E_(i,lambda), and E_(lambda,lambda)Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_(lambda,j).

All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. Under iota, M_R identifies with the internal direct sum of J e_i over i in I; Q tensor_R J has rational dimension one and its multiplication map into C is injective. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.

1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.
183: 
184: ## Input status
185: 
186: This file fixes the exercise, notation and supplied proof, including the
187: arbitrary-lattice argument. It is not an NL0 artifact, an Audit A receipt,
188: a Lean proof, or a passing test result. Future runs must construct and check
189: those artifacts from these explicit inputs, registering any foundational
190: module or localization results used by their NL0.

1: import Mathlib
2: universe u v
3: open scoped TensorProduct
4: open Module
5: attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing
6: noncomputable section
7: namespace Reduction
8: def loc (p : ℕ) : Subring ℚ :=
9:   Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (d : ℚ)⁻¹}
10: instance locComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (loc p) ℂ :=
11:   ((Rat.castHom ℂ).comp (loc p).subtype).toAlgebra
12: abbrev Ind (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
13: abbrev MR {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
14:   (loc p) ⊗[ℤ] M
15: abbrev VK {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) :=
16:   K ⊗[ℤ] M
17: variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
18: instance locModule (p : ℕ) : Module (loc p) V := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (loc p) ℂ)
19: instance locTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℂ V := ⟨fun _ _ _ => mul_smul _ _ _⟩
20: def iota (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M →ₗ[loc p] V :=
21:   LinearMap.liftBaseChange (loc p) M.subtype
22: 
23: abbrev SL := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
24: def divided (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
25:   ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • a ^ r
26: def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := divided y i v
27: def stable {A W : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
28:     (U : Submodule A W) (f : Module.End A W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
29: def matrixUnit {A W ι : Type*} [Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid W] [Module A W]
30:     (b : Basis ι A W) (i j : ι) : Module.End A W :=
31:   LinearMap.smulRight (b.coord j) (b i)
32: def Jcoord (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
33:     Submodule (loc p) ℂ :=
34:   (iota p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[loc p] ℂ) (e y v i))
35: structure IntegralOps (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) where
36:   ix : Module.End ℤ M
37:   iy : Module.End ℤ M
38:   ih : Module.End ℤ M
39:   iX : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
40:   iY : ℕ → Module.End ℤ M
41:   ix_spec : ∀ m : M, (ix m : V) = x m
42:   iy_spec : ∀ m : M, (iy m : V) = y m
43:   ih_spec : ∀ m : M, (ih m : V) = h m
44:   iX_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iX r m : V) = divided x r m
45:   iY_spec : ∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), (iY r m : V) = divided y r m
46: def admissible (M : Submodule ℤ V) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
47:   (∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (a : Basis ι ℤ M) (b : Basis ι ℂ V),
48:     ∀ i, (a i : V) = b i) ∧
49:   (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), divided x r m ∈ M ∧ divided y r m ∈ M)
50: def highestModule (l : ℤ) (act : SL →ₗ⁅ℂ⁆ Module.End ℂ V) (x h : SL) : Prop :=
51:   FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧ Nontrivial V ∧
52:   (∀ U : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ z : SL, stable U (act z)) → U = ⊥ ∨ U = ⊤) ∧
53:   ∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ act x w = 0 ∧ act h w = (l : ℂ) • w
54: def chevalley (x y h : SL) : Prop :=
55:   IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x, y, h} : Set SL) = ⊤
56: def strings (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
57:   (∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • (y ^ t) v) ∧
58:   ∀ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → x ((y ^ t) v) =
59:     ((t : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • (y ^ (t - 1)) v
60: def generatorFormulas {A W : Type*} [Field A] [AddCommGroup W] [Module A W]
61:     (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End A W) (f : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
62:   x (f 0) = 0 ∧
63:   (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → x (f (i+1)) = ((l : A) - (i : A)) • f i) ∧
64:   (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → y (f i) = ((i : A) + 1) • f (i+1)) ∧
65:   y (f l.toNat) = 0 ∧
66:   (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → h (f i) = ((l : A) - 2 * (i : A)) • f i)
67: def basisFacts (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
68:   0 ≤ l ∧ 0 < l + 1 ∧ 0 < l.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Ind l) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
69:   (∃ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) ∧
70:   strings l x y h v ∧
71:   (∀ t : ℕ, l.toNat + 1 ≤ t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧
72:   generatorFormulas l x y h (e y v) ∧
73:   (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
74:     divided x r (e y v i.val) =
75:       if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat - i.val + r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
76:   (∀ (r : ℕ) (i : Ind l),
77:     divided y r (e y v i.val) =
78:       if i.val + r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : ℂ) • e y v (i.val+r) else 0)
79: 
80: instance locRatComplexTower (p : ℕ) : IsScalarTower (loc p) ℚ ℂ :=
81:   IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
82: def locSpec (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
83:   ∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ loc p ↔ ∃ a d : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (d : ℚ)
84: def latticeFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
85:   locSpec p ∧ Nonempty (IntegralOps x y h M) ∧
86:   (∀ A : IntegralOps x y h M,
87:     A.ih * A.ix - A.ix * A.ih = (2 : ℤ) • A.ix ∧
88:     A.ih * A.iy - A.iy * A.ih = (-2 : ℤ) • A.iy ∧
89:     A.ix * A.iy - A.iy * A.ix = A.ih) ∧
90:   Function.Injective (iota p M) ∧
91:   Nonempty (Basis (Ind l) (loc p) (MR p M)) ∧
92:   Module.finrank (loc p) (MR p M) = l.toNat + 1 ∧
93:   Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (iota p M)) = ⊤ ∧
94:   ∀ (r : ℕ) (z : V), z ∈ (iota p M).range →
95:     divided x r z ∈ (iota p M).range ∧ divided y r z ∈ (iota p M).range
96: def matrixFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
97:   ∀ b : Basis (Ind l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = e y v i.val) →
98:   ∀ i j : Ind l,
99:     IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : loc p) ∧
100:     (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℚ)⁻¹ ∈ loc p ∧
101:     (∀ z ∈ (iota p M).range, matrixUnit b i j z ∈ (iota p M).range) ∧
102:     matrixUnit b i j = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹ •
103:       (divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat * divided y (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
104:     divided y l.toNat * divided x l.toNat = matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
105:     divided x (l.toNat-i.val) * matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) =
106:       matrixUnit b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
107:     matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) * divided y (l.toNat-j.val) =
108:       (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • matrixUnit b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
109: def localizationFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
110:   latticeFacts p l x y h M ∧ matrixFacts p l x y v M
111: def coordinateFacts (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
112:   (∀ i : Ind l, Jcoord p M y v i.val = Jcoord p M y v 0) ∧
113:   Jcoord p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (Jcoord p M y v 0).FG ∧
114:   ∃ d : (Ind l → Jcoord p M y v 0) ≃ₗ[loc p] (iota p M).range,
115:     ∀ c, (d c : V) = ∑ i : Ind l, (c i : ℂ) • e y v i.val
116: def rationalMu (p : ℕ) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
117:     ℚ ⊗[loc p] (Jcoord p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
118:   LinearMap.liftBaseChange ℚ (Jcoord p M y v 0).subtype

argument.text: Choose such a basis a from F001. argument.text: Fix i,j in I. The basis formulas in N001 give Q=Y_lambda X_lambda=E_(lambda,lambda): X_lambda kills e_k for k<lambda and sends e_lambda to e_0, which Y_lambda sends back to e_lambda. argument.text: Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. On pure tensors their two composites are the identity, hence on every tensor by linearity.

argument.text: Set r=dim_Q T, a finite natural number by F002. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=Q and source module M_R. Apply M001 over Q to the constant family T indexed by I. F002 supplies finite dimensionality and hence a finite basis of T, while N001 supplies |I|=n. Thus dim_Q(T^I)=sum_(i in I)r=nr. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

Each J_i is an R-submodule, and multiplication by e_i identifies it with the image of the R-linear projection E_ii on the finite free module iota(M_R). Images of a finite generating set generate the image, so J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if every coordinate projection were zero, all of iota(M_R) would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and dim V=n>0. Finally a vector in iota(M_R) is the sum of its E_ii projections, all in J e_i, and conversely every such finite sum belongs to iota(M_R); independence of the e_i makes this sum direct.

Define T=Q tensor_R J. Its multiplication map mu:T->C sends q tensor c to qc. It is injective by the fraction description of localization: any element is a finite sum of pure tensors, and a common nonzero integer denominator d rewrites it as (1/d) tensor c' for some c' in J, because d times each rational coefficient belongs to Z, hence R. If its product in C vanishes, c'=0, so the tensor is zero. This also exhibits Q as the fraction field of R and realizes T as the localization of the torsion-free module J inside C. The images 1 tensor c of a finite generating set of J span T over Q, so T is finite dimensional. Tensoring the finite direct decomposition in F001 gives Q tensor_R M_R isomorphic to product_(i in I)T: the forward map consists of tensoring each coordinate c e_i -> c, and the inverse adds the coordinate inclusions c -> c e_i. The isomorphism in F002 now gives n=nr; n>0 by N001, whence r=1. Together with injectivity of mu, J therefore spans a one-dimensional rational line in C.

F001 and F003 imply existence of a nonzero a in J and a nonempty finite list of nonzero rational scalars q_1,...,q_k for which q_1 a,...,q_k a generate J over R: start with any nonzero a in J, use the one-dimensional rational span to express a finite generating list as rational multiples of a, and discard zero entries. N002 makes iota an isomorphism onto its image, which supplies the equivalent R-basis of M_R. By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. For any integer r with 0<=r<=lambda, H003 and H001 imply p does not divide r!, so H002 gives r! !=0 in K. The equality r! X_r=x^r on V restricts to the same equality on M by N002 and reduces to r! Choose a basis beta and endomorphisms T with the full properties of N004. In particular dim_K V_K=n>0, so V_K is nonzero.

Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V_K and assume L1: W is invariant under x_K,y_K,h_K. It is then invariant under each nonnegative power of x_K and y_K, including power zero, and under their K-scalar multiples. value.N002: M is stable under X_r,Y_r for every natural r, under x,y,h, and these restricted operators satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y and xy-yx=h. iota embeds M_R into V; M_R is free over R of rank n and iota(M_R) complex-linearly spans V. For i,j in I, binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R; the operators E_ij preserve iota(M_R) and satisfy E_ij=binom(lambda,j)^(-1) X_(lambda-i) Y_lambda X_lambda Y_(lambda-j). value.N003: All J_i for i in I equal J. J is a nonzero finitely generated R-submodule of C. There exists a complex scalar b!=0 such that b belongs to J, J=R b, and (b e_i)_{i in I} is an R-basis of iota(M_R), equivalently its inverse images form an R-basis of M_R.
value.N004: There exists a K-basis beta=(beta_i)_{i in I} of V_K, so dim_K V_K=n=lambda+1>0. It has generator matrices x_K beta_0=0; x_K beta_i=(lambda-i+1)beta_(i-1) for 1<=i<=lambda; y_K beta_i=(i+1)beta_(i+1) for i<lambda; y_K beta_lambda=0; h_K beta_i=(lambda-2i)beta_i. 25: /-- `ModN G n` denotes the quotient of `G` by multiples of `n` -/
26: abbrev ModN : Type _ := G ⧸ LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)

33: /-- The universal property of `ModN G n` in terms of monoids: Monoid homomorphisms from `ModN G n`
34: are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
35: protected def liftEquiv [AddMonoid M] : (ModN G n →+ M) ≃ {φ : G →+ M // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} where
36:   toFun f := ⟨f.comp (QuotientAddGroup.mk' _), fun g ↦ by
37:     let Gn : AddSubgroup G := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).toAddSubgroup
38:     suffices n • g ∈ (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn).ker by
39:       simp only [AddMonoidHom.coe_comp, comp_apply, ← map_nsmul]
40:       change f (QuotientAddGroup.mk' Gn (n • g)) = 0 -- Can we avoid `change`?
41:       rw [this, map_zero]
42:     simp [QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk', Gn]⟩
43:   invFun φ := QuotientAddGroup.lift _ φ <| by rintro - ⟨g, rfl⟩; simpa using φ.property g
44:   left_inv f := by
45:     ext x
46:     induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on
47:     rfl -- Should `simp` suffice here?
48:   right_inv φ := by aesop

51: `ModN G n` are the same as monoid homomorphisms from `G` whose values are `n`-torsion. -/
52: protected def liftEquiv' [AddCommGroup H] [Module (ZMod n) H] :
53:     (ModN G n →ₗ[ZMod n] H) ≃ {φ : G →+ H // ∀ g, n • φ g = 0} :=
54:   (AddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMapEquiv n).symm.toEquiv.trans ModN.liftEquiv

57: /-- The quotient map `G → G / nG`. -/
58: def mkQ : G →+ ModN G n := (LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)).mkQ

60: variable [NeZero n]
61: 
62: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
63: /-- Given a free module `G` over `ℤ`, construct the corresponding basis
64: of `G / ⟨n⟩` over `ℤ / nℤ`. -/
65: noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) : Basis ι (ZMod n) (ModN G n) := by
66:   set ψ : G →+ G := zsmulAddGroupHom n
67:   set nG := LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lsmul ℤ G n)
68:   set H := G ⧸ nG
69:   set φ : G →ₗ[ℤ] H := nG.mkQ
70:   let mod : (ι →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := mapRange.linearMap (Int.castAddHom _).toIntLinearMap
71:   let f : G →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ℤ) := b.repr
72:   have hker : nG ≤ LinearMap.ker (mod.comp f) := by
73:     rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩
74:     ext b
75:     simp [mod, f]
76:   let g : H →ₗ[ℤ] (ι →₀ ZMod n) := nG.liftQ (mod.comp f) hker
77:   refine ⟨.ofBijective (g.toAddMonoidHom.toZModLinearMap n) ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
78:   · rw [AddMonoidHom.coe_toZModLinearMap, LinearMap.toAddMonoidHom_coe, injective_iff_map_eq_zero,
79:       nG.mkQ_surjective.forall]
80:     intro x hx
81:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply, g] at hx
82:     rw [Submodule.liftQ_apply] at hx
83:     replace hx : ∀ b, ↑n ∣ f x b := by
84:       simpa [mod, DFunLike.ext_iff, ZMod.intCast_zmod_eq_zero_iff_dvd] using! hx
85:     simp only [Submodule.mkQ_apply]
86:     rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
87:     choose c hc using hx
88:     refine ⟨b.repr.symm ⟨(f x).support, c, by simp [hc, NeZero.ne]⟩, b.repr.injective ?_⟩
89:     simpa [DFunLike.ext_iff, eq_comm] using! hc
90:   · suffices mod ∘ b.repr = g ∘ nG.mkQ by
91:       exact (this ▸ (mapRange_surjective _ (map_zero _) ZMod.intCast_surjective).comp
92:         b.repr.surjective).of_comp
93:     ext x b
94:     simp [mod, g, f, H]
95: 
96: set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
97: lemma basis_apply_eq_mkQ {ι : Type*} (b : Basis ι ℤ G) (i : ι) : basis b i = mkQ n (b i) := by
98:   rw [Basis.apply_eq_iff]; simp [basis, mkQ]

argument.text: By H001-H002, an integer denominator not divisible by p has nonzero image in K and therefore an inverse. Thus the integer map extends uniquely to bar:R->K, bar(a/d)=a_K/d_K. Define Phi:V_K->M_R tensor_R K by m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c; define its inverse on pure tensors by (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor (bar(s)c). The tensor balancing relations make these well-defined K-linear maps, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence on all elements. Since p maps to zero, define Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K by u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c; its inverse sends [u] tensor c to u tensor c. Changing u by p times a vector changes this by zero, and the F_p balancing relation follows from the R balancing relation and bar modulo p. Conversely R/pR=F_p because every denominator is prime to p, so every R scalar has the same reduction as an element of F_p. These maps are mutually inverse on pure tensors. N002 supplies preservation of M by all lattice operators, and H005 their Chevalley relations, so the actions rho and the operators X_K,Y_K are well-defined and all these tensor maps commute with them.

Phi:V_K -> M_R tensor_R K is the K-linear isomorphism m tensor c |-> (1 tensor m) tensor c, with inverse (s tensor m) tensor c |-> m tensor bar(s)c. Psi:M_R tensor_R K -> (M_R/pM_R) tensor_(F_p) K is the K-linear isomorphism u tensor c |-> [u] tensor c, with inverse [u] tensor c |-> u tensor c. These isomorphisms intertwine rho and X_K,Y_K.

The a_i form an R-basis by N002-N003. Its coordinate maps and the map (c_i) -> sum_i a_i tensor c_i are inverse K-linear maps between K^I and M_R tensor_R K; on each pure tensor this is precisely the coordinate expansion. Hence the beta_i form a K-basis. Likewise reducing the coordinates modulo p shows that the classes of a_i form an F_p-basis of M_R/pM_R, whose scalar extension gives this same basis via Psi. N001 gives |I|=n=lambda+1>0. Thus dim_K V_K=n>0.

N002 gives preservation of iota(M_R) by E_ij. Define T_ij by the induced lattice action after pulling back through iota and extending scalars using Phi; then T_ij beta_k=beta_i if k=j and 0 otherwise.
